 United Breweries gets BIADA nod to restore 42-acre Bihar land allotment 
 The restoration follows the company's application under Bihar's Amnesty Policy 2025 after the industrial authority cancelled the original allotment in 2022 over non-operational status and non-utilisation of the land. Online Desk

 United Breweries Ltd (UBL) has received final approval from the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) for restoration of its 42-acre leasehold land at Kopakalan Industrial Area in Patna under the state's Amnesty Policy 2025 . The company disclosed the development in a regulatory filing dated November 14 under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India 's (SEBI) Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015. UBL was allotted Plot No. A-1, measuring 42 acres, by BIADA in 2011 to establish a brewery . The unit subsequently commenced operations. However, following the implementation of Bihar's prohibition policy, the company was forced to discontinue beer production and later secured approval to change the product category from beer to non-alcoholic beverages . During periodic inspections, BIADA found the unit to be non-operational. The authority subsequently cancelled the land allotment and lease in 2022, citing the unit's non-operational status and non-utilisation of the allotted land. UBL challenged the cancellation before the Patna High Court, which passed a status quo order concerning the land. The proceedings remained pending before the court. Subsequently, following the introduction of BIADA's Amnesty Policy 2025, UBL applied for restoration of the allotment, submitted the requisite documents and compliances, and withdrew its writ proceedings. BIADA has now issued an office order restoring the allotment, subject to specified conditions. These include submission of a compliance and acceptance letter within 15 days, achieving trial production within 18 months and commercial production within 24 months. The company is also required to obtain the necessary statutory approvals, furnish details of project financing and implementation, pay applicable charges and comply with BIADA's conditions governing land utilisation. The restoration will entail annual land lease charges of ₹14.62 lakh and facilities charges of ₹70,800, in addition to restoration costs, the company said. UBL added that the communication formally conveys BIADA's approval for restoration and sets out the conditions to be fulfilled by the company. Comments
